subject: Post-call recap: Aurora Health decision criteria & procurement path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>, Mike Jenkins <mike.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Aurora Health decision criteria & procurement path

Hi Elena / Mike —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to flag next steps: 

Key decision criteria you mentioned:
- Data residency & auditability (SOC2 + customer-managed KMS) — must have
- Predictable per-token economics at scale (forecast for 50M tokens/mo) — important
- Low 95th-percentile latency for clinical assistant flows (<300ms target) — preferred
- Integration with existing SSO and logging pipelines (SAML + Splunk) — must have

Stakeholder map (what you told us today):
- Economic buyer: Elena Soto (VP Product) — owns budget and timeline
- Security/Compliance: Mike Jenkins (Head of InfoSec) — will drive SOC2/HIPAA checklist
- Procurement: procurement@aurorahealth.com — formal PO and contract redlines
- Champion / Day-to-day owner: Dr. Priya Menon (Clinical AI product) — will run pilots

Immediate asks we heard on the call: 
- Provide SOC2/HIPAA evidence and a brief on how Redwood handles PHI (for Mike) — action: Naomi to send RFI answers and SOC2 summary (attached)
- Share a compact pricing sheet for a pilot (25k tokens/day) and estimated run rate at 50M tokens/mo — action: Priyom to propose MVP pricing and unit economics
- Draft a simple mutual action plan with milestones for pilot → evaluation → procurement signoff — action: Ben to draft

Attachments: I’m attaching our RFI answers and a starter pricing workbook (see filenames below).

Next internal coordination: Ben / Priyom / Marissa — can we do a 30-min prep tomorrow to align margins and the 90-day pilot success metrics we’ll propose to Elena? Please reply with availability.

Elena / Mike — if anything above is off, please correct. Otherwise we’ll follow up with the RFI + pricing by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments:

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurorahealth.com>

Cc: Mike Jenkins <mike.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Aurora Health decision criteria & procurement path

Thanks Naomi — this looks right and appreciated for the recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) On data residency: we prefer customer-managed KMS in our AWS account. If that’s not supported we need a clear compensating control and contract language.
2) On latency: the 300ms for clinical assistant is for the in-app suggest flow (short prompts). For chart summarization (longer context) the SLAs are lower priority.
3) Procurement timeline: our typical path is pilot acceptance → security signoff → CIO finance approval → PO. Aim to have a procurement-ready commercial term sheet with standard Redwood legal exceptions called out.

Also looping in Dr. Priya Menon (cc’d on a follow-up separately) as the clinical champion to start building acceptance criteria for the pilot.

Elena
VP Product, Aurora Health
elena.soto@aurorahealth.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

> 2) On latency: the 300ms for clinical assistant is for the in-app suggest flow (short prompts). For chart summarization (longer context) the SLAs are lower priority.
> 3) Procurement timeline: our typical path is pilot acceptance → security signoff → CIO finance approval → PO. Aim to have a procurement-ready commercial term sheet with standard Redwood legal exceptions called out.

Thanks for the confirm, Elena. Naomi / Ben — I’ve attached a compact pricing workbook that models pilot costs plus two ramp scenarios (25k tokens/day pilot; 50M tokens/mo steady-state). I also added a recommended pilot SLOs section (latency targets, uptime, and qualitative clinical acceptance checks) in the second sheet.

Action items I’ll take:
- Finalize the MVP pricing sheet with a suggested discount band for a 90-day pilot.
- Draft a two-page legal touchpoints doc listing the minimum contract asks for KMS/PHI handling and the most common redlines we see.

Naomi — for the mutual action plan I suggest we propose:
- Week 0–2: technical onboarding + sample dataset ingest (non-PHI)
- Week 3–6: pilot run with 2 clinicians; weekly demo & feedback loop
- Week 7–8: security review + evidence handoff
- Week 9–12: acceptance criteria run and procurement decision

I’m free 10–11am PT tomorrow for a quick alignment call.

Priyom

priyom.das@redwood.com

Thanks Priyom and Elena for the quick turn. Confirming the 10am PT sync tomorrow (calendar invite to follow). Goals for the 30-min call:
- Lock pilot pricing and discount band we offer for 90-day proof of value
- Agree on the pilot success metrics (uptime, 95p latency for suggest flows, clinician Net Promoter style score after 4 weeks)
- Finalize the two-page legal touchpoints so we can hand to legal for redline ready language

Ben: please bring a short slide with the proposed commercial terms + any promotion approvals you need from leadership. Marissa: can you prep the draft mutual action plan and highlight any SLO gaps we should call out up-front?

I’ll compile the items and send the external follow-up (with attachments) after the internal sync.
